topics.flagship-ru-ua: Russian strikes on critical infrastructure caused hours-long power and water outages in Kyiv and surrounding areas, while rescuers were still searching for survivors in the south (4 outlets). Ukraine and Russia reportedly traded hundreds of drones overnight, with a power substation hit in the Kyiv region, and a Russian guided-bomb strike on Kramatorsk hromada killed two women. Zelensky awarded Melania Trump Ukraine's highest award after an Oleshky ceasefire, and Russian and Ukrainian delegations are due to meet the US first lady at the White House on Thursday. One outlet reports Russia is suspected of hoax bomb threats that grounded UK planes and closed European airports; this is a suspicion, not an established finding.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that US hostility would persist regardless of which party holds power, and he reportedly warned of a wider Middle East war if US attacks continue (3 outlets). After Democrats won the House and Senate, Trump said it was 'largely true' that fuel prices from the Iran war contributed to the loss, but he stood by his decision. Four outlets cite a New York Times report that Israel privately warned Iran is considering chemical weapons use, though not everyone in the US security establishment is convinced. Brent fell about 3% to $100.60 as traders bet on a US-Iran deal. In Gaza, the Education Ministry says Israeli strikes killed a schoolgirl and one person at a university college, and injured 14 students.
topics.T15: Coverage is sparse and generic: a Philippine quake drill by OCD CALABARZON and explainers for World Tsunami Awareness Day on November 5. No actual disaster or access-denial event is reported.
topics.T01: Houthi health authorities say at least seven people, including two children, were killed in an airstrike on Taiz, Yemen, on Wednesday (1 outlet). A separate single-source item reports Yemen's health ministry condemning a Saudi airstrike on a hospital in Ta'iz; the two reports are not confirmed to be the same event. Two outlets report Sudan demanding UN accountability over deadly RSF drone attacks that expose tensions with Ethiopia, and two report a former US contractor admitted passing classified intelligence to Ethiopia that officials used in military operations.
topics.T02: Coverage is too thin to summarize meaningfully: the only item is a profile of Khaled Hosseini's foundation, which supports vulnerable people in Afghanistan.
topics.T04: Anthrax is reportedly killing hippos in the DRC (2 outlets), amid concern about human spread while the country also faces ongoing Ebola and cholera outbreaks. The DRC Ebola outbreak has passed 10,000 cases, and UK officials rate the risk to Britain as low. Kenya discharged five recovered Ebola patients and released 46 contacts from quarantine, while Nigeria is urged to keep up measures after a recent case in Abuja. Animal-health items include Namibia suspending meat exports over foot-and-mouth disease and a second New World screwworm case in southern Arizona.
topics.T05: Reporting is scattered across unrelated countries. In Bangladesh, Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury was arrested in a July Uprising murder case (2 outlets). Poland is reported to be in a constitutional crisis after a senior judge suspended the Constitutional Tribunal president. In Malawi, opposition figure Bon Kalindo suspended planned anti-government protests, giving the government two weeks to address grievances. In the UK, the family of Henry Nowak criticized riots over his killing.
topics.T06: Single-source reporting continues on the French riots that followed an October 17 student protest, including claims that an 'ultra left' faction fueled them and a suspect in a fire at Limoges's city hall. One outlet reports that the presumed organizer of a French-inspired 'Blocus' riot movement in Spain, linked to the October 24 Barcelona riots, allegedly travelled to France beforehand. A Bangladesh item covers the arrest of a death row convict who escaped prison during the July 2024 uprising.
topics.T07: Coverage is thin and opinion-driven, with no outlets counted as independent carriers: analysis of what a US strike on Iran's Pickaxe Mountain facility could look like, and a report that calls for Iran to drop its religious ban on nuclear weapons are moving from the fringe to the mainstream. No new nuclear event is described.
topics.T08: A Jordanian Public Security Directorate corporal was killed in a stabbing attack described as terrorist, and a police officer was injured during the arrest (1 outlet). A Nigerian cleric alleges, based on claimed intelligence reports, a plot to attack Plateau State Christian communities at Christmas; this is unverified. Other items include a Russian teenager detained over neo-Nazi threats against a Moscow museum, the global spread of the banned UK group Palestine Action, and a US court allowing service of a lawsuit on Ahlam Tamimi via X.
topics.T10: South Korea launched a Defense Drone Agency to oversee military drones and reduce reliance on foreign manufacturers. The New York Times reportedly says the Trump administration is negotiating a Status of Forces Agreement with Venezuela that could allow a long-term US military presence (1 outlet). A lawsuit alleges Hegseth's 'Future of Warfare' panel includes 19 private-sector members out of 21. Other items are opinion or market analysis on Golden Dome and defense supply chains.
topics.T11: The US and India began the Tiger Triumph 2026 exercise in Visakhapatnam, focused on humanitarian assistance, disaster response and operational coordination (2 outlets). INS Sahyadri concluded an India-South Korea naval exercise at Busan. One outlet mentions a 10-country European exercise simulating deployment to Ukraine, with the figure of 2,800 troops cited in a sarcastic post-ceasefire framing.
topics.T12: Hackers changed the temperature settings on freezers the French Blood Establishment uses for blood plasma to 110°C instead of -30°C, but staff caught it before any plasma supply was damaged (4 outlets). It is described as the latest attack on cooling companies, following cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration in Germany, Romania and the UK. The EU says the supermarket hacks in at least 11 countries are 'not isolated', while a Romanian official suspects no state actor. Britain's cybersecurity chief said such disruptions are likely to become more frequent as old technology fails to keep pace.
topics.T13: Coverage is mostly political commentary rather than new events: Ceuta presenting a 2027 'war budget' after a late-July mass migrant influx (1 outlet), Farage's citizenship-revocation pledge, Merkel's remarks on Syrians, and a former Border Patrol chief saying the US border is unusually quiet.
topics.T14: The US Embassy in Saudi Arabia reportedly issued a security alert warning of possible Houthi attacks and airport disruptions in Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam, citing recent Houthi hostilities against civilian infrastructure (1 outlet). Separately, a poster at an Iranian rally reportedly threatened to kill Trump.
topics.T16: Democrats won both the House and Senate in the US midterms, and Trump acknowledged that Iran-war fuel prices affected the outcome (multiple outlets). JD Vance also blamed the war for the losses. Markets reacted, with clean-energy stocks up and AI data center and defense-related stocks down. Israeli President Herzog accepted certified election results after a commission denied voter fraud claims and will begin consultations on forming a government.
